subject: CPRA role clarity + onshore-fallback clause for GreenStandard
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greenstandard.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenStandard Contracts <contracts@greenstandard.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CPRA classification + fallback language question

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the product walk-through yesterday. Legal has a narrow set of asks before we can progress to PO: a short confirmation that Redwood will accept "service provider" (CPRA) handling for our use case, plus an onshore-fallback / routing clause in case a subprocessor would otherwise process data offshore.

Two quick questions:
- Can Redwood commit to the standard CPRA "service provider" limitations (no selling, limited use) for GreenStandard?
- Do you have a short fallback sentence we can put into our addendum that guarantees data will be routed to and processed in the U.S. if an offshore subprocessor is unavailable or otherwise unacceptable? We want a one-paragraph fallback we can attach to the MSA.

If it helps, the initial scope is analytics + embeddings for customer support (low PII). Happy to loop in contracts if you prefer.

Cheers,
Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Legal
GreenStandard Inc.

[attachment: requirements-summary.pdf]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greenstandard.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA classification + fallback language question

Sara —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front:
- Yes, we treat CPRA-regulated data under our addendum as a "Service Provider" (limited use, no selling) by default for hosted customers.
- We can provide an onshore-fallback clause that commits to routing and processing within the U.S. if an offshore subprocessor cannot be used.

I'm looping in Priyom (privacy) and Laura (contracts) to confirm the exact one-paragraph language and any operational constraints (e.g., capacity, lead time for onboarding onshore fallback). I'll attach a quick draft in a follow-up.

Next steps:
1) Priyom / Laura: can you confirm if we need any footprint/commitment limits (e.g., traffic caps or SLA exceptions) for the clause?
2) Sara: are you ok with a 30-day lead time for an onshore fallback activation (we can discuss shorter timelines for enterprise commitments)?

Attachment: Redwood-CPRA-SP-draft.docx (draft redline)

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Suggested CPRA paragraph + operational notes

Aditya / Laura —

Draft language that should be acceptable to most midmarket customers (keeps the CPRA "service provider" model but adds an operational fallback):

"If, due to technical, compliance or contractual constraints, Redwood Inference or its authorized subprocessors would otherwise process Covered Data outside the United States, Redwood shall (i) notify Customer promptly and (ii) provide commercially reasonable efforts to route and process such Covered Data within the United States. If within thirty (30) days Redwood is unable to provide onshore processing, Redwood shall (at Customer's election) either (a) suspend the processing of Covered Data that would be routed offshore until onshore processing is available, or (b) delete such Covered Data per Customer instructions."

Operational notes:
- 30 days is reasonable for an onshore fallback that requires provisioning capacity into dedicated pools; for hosted/shared models we can often prioritize within 7–14 days but cannot guarantee sustained throughput without a committed capacity arrangement.
- We should include a short carve-out for emergency security patches/incident response where limited cross-border routing may occur for mitigation; include logging and notification requirements.
- Suggested attachment: onshore-fallback-suggested-clauses.txt (contains incident carve-out and sample SLA language).

Let me know if you want the wording tweaked to be stricter (e.g., 7 days, guaranteed throughput) — stricter timelines typically require a Dedicated/Reserved capacity commitment.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Privacy and Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed CPRA addendum excerpt and next steps

Sara —

Thanks for the patience. Below is the proposed one-paragraph fallback to add to the CPRA addendum; Priyom has confirmed the operational constraints.

>>> Proposed excerpt:
"If, due to technical, compliance, or contractual constraints, Redwood Inference or its authorized subprocessors would otherwise process Covered Data outside the United States, Redwood shall (i) notify Customer promptly and (ii) provide commercially reasonable efforts to route and process such Covered Data within the United States. If within thirty (30) days Redwood is unable to provide onshore processing, Redwood shall (at Customer's election) either (a) suspend the processing of Covered Data that would be routed offshore until onshore processing is available, or (b) delete such Covered Data per Customer instructions."

Operational summary (for your contracts team):
- Default CPRA stance: Service Provider, limited use, no selling.
- Onshore fallback: 30-day SLA to prioritize onshore processing. For stronger SLAs (7–14 days) we recommend a Dedicated/Reserved capacity commitment.
- Emergency carve-out: limited routing for incident response with notification and logging.

Attachments sent: Redwood-CPRA-SP-draft.docx (redline with the excerpt), onshore-fallback-suggested-clauses.txt (carve-out + suggested SLAs).

If GreenStandard is comfortable with the paragraph, I can get Laura to prepare a short addendum and we can route it for signature (DocuSign). Otherwise, let me know if you want a shorter timeline and we can discuss the Dedicated pricing path.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
